scope: Native email change requests and ordinary-user suggestion support

primaryDocumentation.supports: An authenticated user can request an email update; secure email change normally confirms both current and proposed addresses.

implementation: PUT auth/v1/user with normalized email and the official website confirmation target, validating returned own user identity in either Auth SDK supported response shape. No pending address is represented as a confirmed native-account change.
Pending new_email is read from the own authenticated auth user and displayed separately. Links are confirmed outside this native UI on the official service.
Own latest20suggestion rows, explicit status and staff reply, observed suggestion_votes aggregate and own thumbs-up/down reaction toggling.

Submission is available only for actual visible text channels named suggestions-new or suggestions in the source-specified official HQ server. No management/staff-list API or fabricated join permission is used.

Form uses source title5–100UTF16 characters, body10–1500, explicit category selection and server-enforced daily limits. In-session draft fields are account/channel bound and cleared on successful submission or account logout.
The existing native channel view lets the user browse and react to other posted suggestions; this screen lists the own history and does not query the staff moderation queue.
knownLimits: Account switching and a multiple-session Keychain vault are not implemented by this checkpoint. No Safari, external browser or other-client session storage is read.

No email or suggestion was actually changed/submitted/voted by the agent. Email delivery, dual-address confirmation, pending-state refresh and account-specific HQ permissions remain runtime-unverified.
Suggestion limits and access are enforced by the existing backend; staff decisions and queue controls are not exposed to ordinary users.

tests.typecheck: Swift6 MainActor iOS17 simulator passed in temporary harness; existing compiled Security symbols aliased in harness only to avoid duplicate imported overloads. Root integrated build remains authoritative.
